findings.text: The claim 'at k=10 and k=30 every returned candidate is EDAS eqread_pac client code' overstates: at k=10, 3 of 10 candidates are not under eqread_pac (eslice_esurf/default/Eqread.py and two eslice_esurf/db/Fledd.py, scores 8.32 and 6.46); at k=30, 10 of 30 are under the eslice_esurf, eslice_eslice2/eslice_plugins/jt60sa, eslice_data_area and egis trees, none under eqread_pac. All are EDAS code, but 'every candidate is eqread_pac client code' is not accurate. The load-bearing claim that the layout's chunks are absent from the pool below k=50 is correct and independently verified.

The fragment records live-graph values (CodeFile status/relevance_stage/score_composite, chunk counts and search ranks) with no revision or timestamp beside them, and the record has already drifted from the live graph within roughly ninety minutes. A review re-read of the reviewed head's own q_verify query at 2026-10-07T09:47Z returns: eqwt13.f skipped/name (fragment: triaged), eqwt2.f skipped/content sc=0.47 (fragment: triaged), and a third ingested reader carrying the _BF field list, /analysis/lib/eqdbms/eqdbget.f (5 _BF chunks), which the fragment's snapshot does not name. The central verdict (the two named readers hold the layout; the criterion misses them) is stable, but the per-file status detail is a point-in-time value. Stamping the counts to the reviewed head would keep the durable record reconcilable with the live graph.

(d) The verdict that the criterion names the right topic but the wrong sources, and that the layout needs fuller ingesting, is stated. (e) The fragment is written and the scripts/logs are in the granted reports directory. (f) No graph write, no code change, no discover run.

justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced, not read. Re-running the reviewed head's own q_verify query against the live graph at 2026-10-07T09:47Z returns the fragment's numbers exactly for the holders: eqdbget2m.f ingested/content/0.54/4 chunks, SAeqread/eqdbget.f ingested/content/0.57/5 chunks, SAeqfame/eqdbget.f ingested/content/0.68/5 chunks; include-file (.bf/#AAA/#GEO/#EQU/#VAC/#MSEDB/#EQ2M) CodeFile rows = 0; JT60SAEQDB CodeFile rows = 0; client_eqdbms.EQ32.Rev1/eqdbms/EQDB = 31 rows all skipped/name; EDAS EQDB eqwt10.f 0.56 and eqwt11.f 0.52 ingested. The search ranks reproduce from the reviewed run's own logs and JSON: k50 order places eqdbget2m.f at #39 (raw score 0.886), EQDB/eqdbio.f at #44 (0.881), SAeqfame/eqdbget.f at #45-46 (0.875), geteddbt.c at #50 (0.861); the rerank JSON re-sorted by its jev score gives #2 SAeqfame/eqdbget.f (2.01), #4 eqdbget2m.f (1.72), #8 EQDB/eqdbio.f (1.52), #9 eqdata_get.f, and the k=30 rerank pool contains no layout chunk (top six are EDAS eqread_pac files). I additionally took the host arm the node was denied: the JT-60SA hop answers now (hostname intr26-2, exit 0), and a bounded read-only find confirms the standalone include files the fragment says the graph lacks, /analysis/src/client_eqdbms.EQ32.Rev1/inc/F/#AAA.bf, #GEO.bf, #EQU.bf, #EQV.bf, #OUT.bf, #PAR.bf, #VAC.bf, #CNT.bf, #EQ2M.bf, #MSEDB.bf, #EQTTL.bf (plus F_1025/F_129 variants), so the fragment's verdict holds and the follow-on to ingest them is actionable with that path. justifications.fit: The fragment follows the repository's evidence-fragment idiom: a single <section>, a node-prefixed h2 id (eqdbms-layout-probe) and node-prefixed element ids, a finding paragraph, a holders paragraph, a what-the-graph-lacks paragraph, a rank paragraph, a host paragraph and a verdict, and a pointer to the off-repo evidence. No plan, sprint or ticket label appears in the committed file, and the record lands as the fragment plus a landing line in the manifest, not a plan edit, as the envelope required.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's goal (locate where the JT-60SA EQDBMS record layout is defined and whether search can find it) is answered at the reviewed head on both halves: the layout's field list is located to the ingested readers and the EDAS EQDB writers with their graph state given, and the search is shown to name the EDAS eqread_pac clients rather than the EQDBMS-library readers/writers, with the defect localised to retrieval (pool size) rather than ranking because the Jev rerank recovers the layout once the pool contains it. Classifying from the graph alone is the arm the fence allows when the hop is down.
justifications.reuse: The node adds no product code and duplicates nothing. It reads the graph through the existing GraphClient and the host through the sanctioned /tmp/sshwrap/ssh wrapper, and its only new artifacts are small read-only probe scripts and their logs in the granted reports directory. No graph write, no code change, no discover run.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 504da5c66..6627d3e11 is one file, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/eqdbms-layout-probe.html, 122 insertions, the single declared in-repo write path. The build also writes only its granted reports directory outside the repo. The granted figure path is unused, which the envelope's own small-node rule and the table-shaped result both support. No plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in the committed file; no AI attribution in the commit.

negative_control_applied: not required: the reviewed node's write paths reach no test path and its manifest declares no negative_control_log; the dispatch envelope itself recorded 'This node declares a mutation, but its write paths reach no test path, so promotion reads no red log for it'. The declared host/graph mutation (the same graph search applied to a field name a returned eqread_pac chunk is known to carry finds that chunk) was not separately re-run, but the reviewed run's own out_verify.txt shows the search procedure returns known-present tokens (EQDBGET in eqdbget_* files, IRDM_BF/IZDM_BF in the readers), so the procedure is shown able to see a present token and the absence of a standalone-definition CodeFile is a real absence.
